chunks: Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

"When it is the Night of Decree, and 'in it is made clear every wise matter,' a caller will cry out that night from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has forgiven whoever visited the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on this night.'"

key_terms.فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ: In it is made clear every wise matter (Quranic reference)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, a blessed night in Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn on Laylat al-Qadr?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the unique intercessory status of Imam al-Husayn (AS) by linking his grave visitation directly to the divine decree of forgiveness on Laylat al-Qadr, a night where every affair is settled. The call emanating from beneath the Throne signifies a direct, audible divine proclamation, elevating the act of Ziyarat from a devotional practice to a means of securing one's fate for the coming year. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the cosmic significance of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the martyr of Karbala, as a locus of divine mercy.
